result.topic_en: Euler discusses which primes of the form 2p+1 can divide a^n − 1 when n shares a divisor with 2p, applies this to the prime divisors of a^3 − 1, a^5 − 1 and Mersenne numbers 2^n − 1, and begins showing that a^n − 1 with n < 2p is not always divisible by 2p+1.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 8. 31
$a^{\nu\beta\lambda+\lambda}-a^{\nu\beta\lambda}=a^{\nu\beta\lambda}(a^{\lambda}-1)$, quae cum sit divisibilis per $2p+1$, necesse est sit $a^{\lambda}-1$ per
$2p+1$ divisibile.
248. Si ergo $n$ sit numerus ad $2p$ primus, forma $a^n-1$ divisibilis esse nequit per numerum
primum $2p+1$, nisi sit $a-1$ per eundem divisibile. Unde si $a-1$ non sit multiplum numeri
primi $2p+1$, formula $a^n-1$ per eum divisibilis esse nequit, nisi $n$ et $2p$ sint numeri inter se
compositi, quorum si maximus communis divisor sit $\lambda$, adeo haec formula $a^{\lambda}-1$ per $2p+1$ erit
divisibilis.
249. Si igitur $a^n$ fuerit minima potestas ipsius $a$, quae per numerum primum $2p+1$ divisa
unitatem relinquit, tum certe est $n$ pars aliquota numeri $2p$. Tum autem si fuerit $ab=k(2p+1)+1$,
erit etiam $b^n$ minima potestas ipsius $b$, quae per $2p+1$ divisa unitatem relinquit.
250. Si $n$ sit numerus primus et formula $a^n-1$ divisibilis per numerum primum $2p+1$,
vel erit $n$ pars aliquota ipsius $2p$ (quia alius communis divisor locum non habet), vel si fuerit ad
$2p$ primus, numerus $a-1$ per $2p+1$ erit divisibilis. Quare praeter divisores ipsius $a-1$ formula
$a^n-1$ alios divisores primos non admittit, nisi hujusmodi formae $2p+1$, ut $2p$ sit multiplum
ipsius $n$. Unde omnes ejus divisores primi in hac forma $2mn+1$ continebuntur.
251. Quare haec forma $a^3-1$ praeter divisorem $a-1$ alios divisores primos non admittit
nisi formae $6m+1$, qui sunt 7, 13, 19, 31, 37, 43, 61, 67, 73, 79, 97 etc. Cum ergo $aa+a+1$
sit factor ipsius $a^3-1$, etiam is per nullos alios numeros primos est divisibilis.
252. Simili modo forma $a^5-1$ praeter divisorem $a-1$ alios non habet, nisi qui in forma
$10m+1$ contineantur, quales sunt 11, 31, 41, 61, 71 etc. Quare etiam tales numeri
$a^4+a^3+a^2+a+1$,
nisi sint primi, alios divisores non admittunt.
253. Quoniam numeri perfecti inveniuntur, quoties formula $2^n-1$ est numerus primus, primum
patet hoc evenire non posse, nisi $n$ sit numerus primus. At si $n$ fuerit talis, formula $2^n-1$ certe
alios non habet divisores nisi formae $2mn+1$, unde exploratio utrum sit primus, nec ne? faciliori
negotio absolvitur.
254. Cum $a^{2p}-1$ semper sit divisibile per numerum primum $2p+1$, illa autem forma constet
factoribus $a^p-1$ et $a^p+1$, necesse est ut alteruter per $2p+1$ sit divisibilis. Vidimus autem,
si sit $a=ee\pm\lambda(2p+1)$, fore $a^p-1$ divisibilem; his ergo casibus formula $a^p+1$ per $2p+1$
certe non est divisibilis.
255. Hic quaestio oritur, num forte semper formula $a^p-1$ per $2p+1$ sit divisibilis? ideoque
nunquam altera $a^p+1$, quod casu, quo $p$ est numerus impar, statim negandum esse patet. Quia
enim tum $a^p+1$ factorem habet $a+1$, ista formula sumto $a=2p$ manifesto per $2p+1$ fit
divisibilis.
256. In genere autem sequenti modo ostendi potest formulam $a^n-1$, existente $n<2p$, non
semper divisibilem esse per numerum primum $2p+1$, sed dari utique ejusmodi numeros pro $a$
adhibendos, quibus divisio formulae $a^n-1$ non succedat, quod per deductionem ad absurdum
sic commodissime demonstrabitur.

methods.what: If a^{m} and a^{m+λ} both leave remainder 1 mod 2p+1, then a^λ − 1 is divisible by 2p+1 (factorization step)
If gcd(n,2p)=1, then prime 2p+1 divides a^n − 1 only if it divides a − 1; in general it divides a^λ − 1 with λ = gcd(n,2p)
methods.quote:
Si ergo $n$ sit numerus ad $2p$ primus, forma $a^n-1$ divisibilis esse nequit per numerum
primum $2p+1$, nisi sit $a-1$ per eundem divisibile.

methods.what: The multiplicative order of a modulo prime 2p+1 divides 2p; if ab ≡ 1, then b has the same order
methods.quote:
Si igitur $a^n$ fuerit minima potestas ipsius $a$, quae per numerum primum $2p+1$ divisa
unitatem relinquit, tum certe est $n$ pars aliquota numeri $2p$. Tum autem si fuerit $ab=k(2p+1)+1$,
erit etiam $b^n$ minima potestas ipsius $b$, quae per $2p+1$ divisa unitatem relinquit.

methods.what: For prime n, prime divisors of a^n − 1 not dividing a − 1 have the form 2mn+1
methods.quote: Unde omnes ejus divisores primi in hac forma $2mn+1$ continebuntur.

methods.what: Prime divisors of a^2+a+1 (beyond those of a − 1) are of the form 6m+1
methods.quote:
Quare haec forma $a^3-1$ praeter divisorem $a-1$ alios divisores primos non admittit
nisi formae $6m+1$, qui sunt 7, 13, 19, 31, 37, 43, 61, 67, 73, 79, 97 etc.

methods.what: Prime divisors of a^4+a^3+a^2+a+1 (beyond those of a − 1) are of the form 10m+1
methods.quote:
Simili modo forma $a^5-1$ praeter divisorem $a-1$ alios non habet, nisi qui in forma
$10m+1$ contineantur, quales sunt 11, 31, 41, 61, 71 etc.

methods.what: 2^n − 1 can be prime only if n is prime; its divisors are then of the form 2mn+1, which simplifies testing Mersenne numbers (connected with perfect numbers)
methods.quote:
At si $n$ fuerit talis, formula $2^n-1$ certe
alios non habet divisores nisi formae $2mn+1$, unde exploratio utrum sit primus, nec ne? faciliori
negotio absolvitur.

methods.what: Since a^{2p} − 1 = (a^p − 1)(a^p + 1), prime 2p+1 divides exactly one factor; if a ≡ square mod 2p+1, it divides a^p − 1, not a^p + 1 (Euler's criterion direction)
methods.quote:
Vidimus autem,
si sit $a=ee\pm\lambda(2p+1)$, fore $a^p-1$ divisibilem; his ergo casibus formula $a^p+1$ per $2p+1$
certe non est divisibilis.

methods.what: Counterexample for odd p: a = 2p gives a+1 | a^p+1, so 2p+1 divides a^p + 1
methods.quote:
Quia
enim tum $a^p+1$ factorem habet $a+1$, ista formula sumto $a=2p$ manifesto per $2p+1$ fit
divisibilis.

Hic quaestio oritur, num forte semper formula $a^p-1$ per $2p+1$ sit divisibilis? ideoque
nunquam altera $a^p+1$
items.english: Here the question arises whether perhaps the formula a^p − 1 is always divisible by 2p+1, and hence never the other one, a^p + 1.

items.quote:
In genere autem sequenti modo ostendi potest formulam $a^n-1$, existente $n<2p$, non
semper divisibilem esse per numerum primum $2p+1$, sed dari utique ejusmodi numeros pro $a$
adhibendos, quibus divisio formulae $a^n-1$ non succedat
items.english: In general, however, it can be shown in the following way that the formula a^n − 1, with n < 2p, is not always divisible by the prime 2p+1, but that there certainly exist numbers to be used for a for which the division of a^n − 1 does not succeed.

items.quote:
quod per deductionem ad absurdum
sic commodissime demonstrabitur.
items.english: which will most conveniently be demonstrated by reduction to absurdity as follows.
